1	# Settings protocol
2	
3	`PUT /settings` accepts a JSON object with one `display_name` member.
4	
5	| Value | Protocol v1 | Protocol v2 |
6	| --- | --- | --- |
7	| String | Store the string after removing leading/trailing Unicode whitespace | Same as v1 |
8	| Empty string (including a whitespace-only string after normalization) | Store an explicit empty label | Same as v1 |
9	| `null` | Return HTTP 422; leave the stored value unchanged | Remove the explicit label; subsequent reads use the account default |
10	
11	Here, surrounding Unicode whitespace means exactly the characters removed by
12	Python's `str.strip()` with no argument. Both provider versions use this same
13	definition and preserve internal whitespace. A successful write returns
14	`{"ok": true}`. A transport returns that response on success and raises on
15	non-success HTTP status. The client receives a borrowed transport; it neither
16	owns the connection nor retries calls. These are versioned protocol semantics,
17	not a record of which version a deployment runs.
